card.name: Ikariotikos
card.era: Traditional island dance; popularized nationally via a 1975 song by Giorgos Konitopoulos
card.tagline: The fast island chain dance of Ikaria.
card.profile: A traditional chain folk dance and accompanying song from the island of Ikaria in the NE Aegean. Danced in an open circle/line, men and women holding hands (older form, crossed palms) or by the shoulders. Structured in parts: slow walking steps (akin to Sta Tria), then steps resembling the Issios of Kalymnos, then fast steps with full leg-and-body mobility; duple 2/4 rhythm. Historically sung, then accompanied by Cretan/island lyra, the Ikarian tsampouna (bagpipe), and violin with laouto/mandolin; today also guitar, bouzouki and accordion. Danced at weddings, baptisms and religious festivals (English Wikipedia; ResearchGate ethnographic study).
card.insight: Some specialists hold that the original Ikariotikos was slow and the fast popular version is effectively a Ballos; its modern fame owes much to Giorgos Konitopoulos's song 'My love in Ikaria,' notably performed by Yiannis Parios (English Wikipedia).

observation.setting: outdoor paved courtyard in front of a brick building with church icons, public performance
observation.dancers: group of mixed teenage dancers, both male and female
observation.formation_and_space: long line of dancers holding hands, curving into a circle and traveling counter-clockwise
observation.footwork: stepping sideways with side-cross or step-hop combinations, shifting weight along with the beat
observation.arms_and_hands: hands held at shoulder height in a line, arms extended to neighbors
observation.hips_and_torso: minimal torso movement, slight bounce from the knees
observation.partnering: none as couple dancing; connected in a line by holding hands/shoulders
observation.levels_jumps_turns: low hops on single beats, occasional pivot turns
observation.costume_and_props: traditional Greek folk costumes: women in white dresses, black or red vests and aprons; men in white fustanella skirts, blue vests, white stockings, and red caps
